slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
ASA: if two angles and the included side of one triangle are equal to two angles and the included side of another, the triangles are congruent.

Why: given angle A = angle D, AB = DE and angle B = angle E. Map A to D and B to E as before, reflecting if needed so C and F are on the same side of DE. Equal angles at A and D put C on ray DF; equal angles at B and E put C on ray EF. Two different rays meet in only one point, so C lands on F.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: In the ASA argument, why does C have to land exactly on F?
slides.reveal: C lies on both ray DF and ray EF, and two rays that are not on the same line meet in at most one point, which is F.
